title: High Molecular Weight DNA Extraction from Recalcitrant Plant Species for Third Generation Sequencing
author: Rachael Workman

steps.title: Prepare 10X Homogenization Buffer
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1.21 g Trizma base, 5.96 g KCl, 20 mL 0.5 M EDTA, 0.255 g Spermidine and 0.348 g Spermine in ddH₂O, adjust the volume to 100 mL, set pH to 9‑9.4 with drops of 10 N NaOH, store at 4 °C in a glass bottle (up to 1 year).

steps.title: Prepare 1X HB Solution
steps.instruction: Mix 100 mL of the 10X HB stock with 171.2 g sucrose, add ddH₂O to 700 mL, stir until dissolved, then bring the final volume to 1 L; store at 4 °C in a glass bottle (up to 3 months).

steps.title: Prepare 20% Triton X‑100 Mix
steps.instruction: Combine 20 mL Triton X‑100, 10 mL 10X HB, and 17.15 g sucrose; add ddH₂O to 60 mL, stir until dissolved, then bring to a final volume of 100 mL; store at 4 °C in a glass bottle (up to 1 year).

steps.title: Make Nuclear Isolation Buffer (NIB)
steps.instruction: Prepare 10 mL NIB per gram of tissue plus an extra 50 mL for washes; for 5 g tissue mix 97.5 mL 1X HB, 2.5 mL Triton X‑100 mix, 250 µL β‑mercaptoethanol (add immediately before use) and 1 g PVP, stir until homogeneous.

steps.title: Grind Tissue and Homogenize in NIB
steps.instruction: Grind 1 g fresh or snap‑frozen tissue to a fine powder in liquid N₂ using a mortar and pestle, transfer the powder to a capped 250 mL bottle containing 10 mL NIB, cap and mix on an end‑over‑end shaker at maximum speed for 15 min at 4 °C. Alternative mixing: place bottles on their side on a shaker at 150 rpm, or transfer the powder to a foil‑capped beaker and stir on a plate with a stir bar at 4 °C for 15 min.

substeps.instruction: Grind tissue in liquid N₂ to a fine powder.
Transfer powder to a capped 250 mL bottle with 10 mL NIB.
Mix on end‑over‑end shaker, max speed, 15 min, 4 °C.
Alternative: shake at 150 rpm or stir plate at 4 °C for 15 min.

steps.title: Filter Homogenate and Centrifuge
steps.instruction: Gravity‑filter the homogenate through five layers of Miracloth into a 50 mL conical tube, cap and centrifuge at 4 °C for 20 min; use 1900 × g for redwood (≈30 Gb), 2500 × g for maize (≈2.5 Gb) or 2900 × g for walnut (≈1 Gb).

substeps.instruction: Filter homogenate through 5 layers of Miracloth into a 50 mL conical tube.
Cap tube and centrifuge at 4 °C for 20 min at the appropriate g‑force (1900 × g for redwood, 2500 × g for maize, 2900 × g for walnut).

steps.title: Resuspend Pellet in Cold NIB
steps.instruction: Decant the supernatant, add 1 mL cold NIB to the pellet and resuspend using a paintbrush pre‑soaked in NIB (pipetting may be ineffective for sticky pellets).

steps.title: Wash Nuclei Suspension and Centrifuge
steps.instruction: Transfer 1 mL of the nuclei suspension to a 15 mL conical tube, bring the volume to 15 mL with ice‑cold NIB, then centrifuge at the same speed and temperature used in step 6 for 10 min.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 1 mL nuclei suspension to a 15 mL conical tube.
Add ice‑cold NIB to reach 15 mL total volume.
Centrifuge at the same g‑force and 4 °C as in step 6 for 10 min.

steps.title: Repeat Wash if Supernatant Colored
steps.instruction: If the supernatant is clear, decant and proceed; if coloration remains, discard the supernatant, resuspend the pellet in 10‑15 mL cold NIB and repeat the centrifugation under the same conditions. For conifer tissue repeat this wash 3‑5 times; for maize it is usually unnecessary.

substeps.instruction: Check supernatant clarity after centrifugation.
If clear: decant supernatant and continue.
If colored: discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 10‑15 mL cold NIB, repeat centrifugation at the same speed and temperature.
For conifer tissue repeat this wash 3‑5 times; maize typically requires no repeat.

steps.title: Resuspend Nuclei in 1X HB
steps.instruction: Remove the supernatant and resuspend the nuclei pellet in 1 mL 1X HB.

steps.title: Choose Snap‑Freeze or Proceed to Lysis
steps.instruction: Option A – Snap‑freeze: spin the nuclei suspension in a 1.5 mL tube at 5000‑7000 × g for 5 min, remove supernatant, snap‑freeze in liquid N₂ and store at –80 °C. Option B – Proceed to lysis: spin under the same conditions, remove supernatant and continue with step 12.

substeps.instruction: Snap‑freeze: centrifuge at 5000‑7000 × g for 5 min, discard supernatant, snap‑freeze nuclei in liquid N₂, store at –80 °C.
Proceed to lysis: centrifuge at 5000‑7000 × g for 5 min, discard supernatant, continue to step 12.

steps.title: Lyse Nuclei with Proteinase K
steps.instruction: Resuspend the nuclei pellet in 30 µL Proteinase K, vortex on high until fully dispersed, then spin 2 s to remove liquid from the cap. Optional: add 10 µL RNase A, pulse‑vortex 5×, spin 2 s and incubate at room temperature (18‑25 °C) for 3 min.

substeps.instruction: Add 30 µL Proteinase K to the nuclei pellet and vortex on high until fully resuspended.
Spin the tube for 2 s to remove liquid from the cap.
Optional RNase treatment: add 10 µL RNase A, pulse‑vortex 5×, spin 2 s, incubate at 18‑25 °C for 3 min.

steps.title: Add Buffer PL1 and Vortex
steps.instruction: Add 80 µL Buffer PL1, pulse‑vortex 10×, spin 2 s; if the mixture appears inhomogeneous, vortex continuously on high for 10 s.

substeps.instruction: Add 80 µL Buffer PL1.
Pulse‑vortex 10× and spin 2 s.
If inhomogeneous, vortex continuously on high for 10 s.

steps.title: Incubate Lysate at 55 °C
steps.instruction: Place the tube on a ThermoMixer set to 55 °C and 900 rpm for 30 min; a mid‑lysis pulse‑vortex (5×) may be performed. If lysate is not fully cleared, extend incubation up to 2 h.

substeps.instruction: Incubate at 55 °C, 900 rpm for 30 min.
Optional: pulse‑vortex 5× during incubation.
If incomplete lysis, increase incubation time up to 2 h.

steps.title: Clarify Lysate by Centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the lysate at 16 000 × g for 5 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Bind DNA to Nanobind Disk
steps.instruction: Transfer the cleared supernatant to a new 1.5 mL Protein LoBind tube using a wide‑bore pipette, add a Nanobind disk, then add isopropanol equal to 1× the supernatant volume (adjust proportionally if volume exceeds 150 µL); always add the disk before the isopropanol.

substeps.instruction: Transfer supernatant to a 1.5 mL Protein LoBind tube with a wide‑bore tip.
Add a Nanobind disk.
Add isopropanol equal to the supernatant volume (1×); if volume >150 µL, scale isopropanol accordingly.

steps.title: Mix Binding Reaction for 20 min
steps.instruction: Mix the tube for 20 min at room temperature by inverting or using a HulaMixer (or 5× inversions every 2‑3 min if a HulaMixer is unavailable); do not use a tube rotator.

substeps.instruction: Invert the tube periodically (or use a HulaMixer) for a total of 20 min at RT.
If no HulaMixer, perform 5 inversions every 2‑3 min.
Avoid using a tube rotator.

steps.title: Magnetic Washes with Buffer PW1
steps.instruction: Place the tube on a magnetic rack, discard the supernatant, add 500 µL Buffer PW1, invert 4×, replace on the magnet and discard supernatant; repeat the PW1 wash, spin 2 s to remove residual liquid, and if the Nanobind disk blocks the tube bottom, gently push it aside with a pipette tip. Continue PW1 washes until the disk and tube appear dry.

substeps.instruction: Place tube on magnetic rack and discard supernatant.
Add 500 µL Buffer PW1, invert 4×, replace on magnet, discard supernatant.
Repeat the PW1 wash.
Spin 2 s to remove residual liquid from the cap.
If the disk blocks the bottom, gently push it aside with a pipette tip.
Repeat PW1 washes until the disk and tube look dry.

steps.title: Elute DNA with Buffer EB
steps.instruction: Add 50‑200 µL Buffer EB, spin 2 s, incubate at room temperature for 10 min ensuring the Nanobind disk is fully immersed; the disk may be gently compressed into the tube bottom with a pipette tip without damage.

substeps.instruction: Add 50‑200 µL Buffer EB.
Spin 2 s and incubate at RT for 10 min with the disk fully submerged.
If needed, gently compress the disk into the tube bottom using a pipette tip.

steps.title: Collect and Store Eluted DNA
steps.instruction: Transfer the eluate to a new 1.5 mL tube using a wide‑bore pipette, spin 5 s, collect any remaining liquid, and repeat if necessary; using a wide‑bore tip helps preserve 50‑300+ kb DNA fragments.

substeps.instruction: Transfer eluate to a fresh 1.5 mL tube with a wide‑bore tip.
Spin 5 s and collect any residual liquid.
Repeat transfer if needed to maximize recovery.

steps.title: Assess DNA Quality
steps.instruction: Measure DNA concentration and purity with a NanoDrop and Qubit; note that high‑molecular‑weight DNA may appear inhomogeneous—leaving the sample at room temperature overnight can improve homogeneity.
